subject: System Design
title: How Google Indexes the Web
description: A quick win: understand How Google Indexes the Web.

hook.text: Google searches billions of pages in under 0.5 seconds. The secret: it doesn't search the web — it searches an index.

buildup.text: Googlebot crawls the web, following links from page to page. It downloads and parses each page's content.

discovery.text: The index is an inverted index: for each word, a list of pages containing it, plus positions and context.

twist.text: The web is mostly junk. Google must decide what to crawl and how often. News sites: every minute. Blogs: weekly.

climax.text: Google's index is one of the largest data structures ever built — hundreds of petabytes of structured web data.

punchline.text: Crawl the web, build an inverted index, search the index — not the web.

quiz.question: What is an inverted index?
options: A data structure mapping each word to the list of pages containing it
A list of all URLs on the internet
A backup copy of the web
